title: Visit Array Positions to Maximize Score
statement:
You are given an integer array `nums` and a positive integer `x`. You begin at index `0`, which already earns you `nums[0]` points. From your current index `i` you may jump forward to any index `j > i`, as many times as you like (possibly never), so you visit an increasing sequence of indices that starts at `0`.

- Every index you visit adds its value `nums[i]` to your score.
- Every jump between two indices whose values have different parity (one even, one odd) subtracts `x` from your score.

Return the largest total score you can finish with.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every set of visited indices is exponential. The only thing that matters about the path so far, when deciding the next step, is the parity of the last value visited: it decides whether stepping onto `nums[i]` costs `x`. So keep two states: the best score of a path that currently ends on an even value, and the best score of one that ends on an odd value. Since every value is positive, visiting an index never hurts a path of the same parity, which keeps the update simple.

## Approach

1. Set `best[0]` and `best[1]` to `-Infinity` (no such path yet), then `best[nums[0] % 2] = nums[0]` for the forced start.
2. For each later index `i`, let `parity = nums[i] % 2`.
3. `stay`: extend the best path that already ends on this parity, at no cost.
4. `change`: extend the best path ending on the other parity and pay `x`.
5. The best path ending at `i` is `max(stay, change) + nums[i]`; store it in `best[parity]`. It is never worse than the old `best[parity]`, because adding a positive value to that path is allowed.
6. Return the larger of the two states.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [2,3,6,1,9,2]`, `x = 5`. Start `best = [2, -Inf]`. `3` (odd): `max(-Inf, 2 - 5) + 3 = 0`, so `best = [2, 0]`. `6`: `max(2, -5) + 6 = 8`, `best = [8, 0]`. `1`: `max(0, 3) + 1 = 4`, `best = [8, 4]`. `9`: `max(4, 3) + 9 = 13`, `best = [8, 13]`. `2`: `max(8, 8) + 2 = 10`, `best = [10, 13]`. The answer is `13`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one constant-time update per index.
- Space: O(1): two numbers.

## Pitfalls

- Index `0` must be visited; do not start both states at `0`, or a path could skip it.
- Start the missing parity at `-Infinity`, not `0`, so a switch from a nonexistent path is never chosen.
- Totals can reach about 10^11, beyond 32-bit integers; Java and C need a 64-bit type.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `best[p]` | best score of a path from index 0 whose last value has parity `p` |
| `parity` | parity of `nums[i]` |
| `stay` | best score arriving from the same parity |
| `change` | best score arriving from the other parity, after paying `x` |

narration.2: No path ends on either parity yet.
narration.3: The path must start at index 0, so its value seeds the state of its parity.
narration.4: Consider each later index as the next place to visit.
narration.5: The value's parity decides which state it extends for free.
narration.6: Coming from a path of the same parity costs nothing.
narration.7: Coming from the other parity costs x.
narration.8: Take the better arrival and add this value; this is the best path ending on this parity now.
narration.10: The best final score ends on either parity.
